prompt: Write the letter informing the International Space Station that it is now a U.S. state. Assign it a football conference.
response:
**THE WHITE HOUSE**
**OFFICE OF INTERGOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS**
**WASHINGTON, D.C.**

*TO: Commander, International Space Station (ISS)*
*FROM: Executive Office of the President of the United States*
*SUBJECT: Official Notification of Statehood and Athletic Realignment*

Dear Commander and Crew,

It is my great honor to officially inform you that, following a swift and highly unconventional midnight vote in the United States Congress, the International Space Station has been formally ratified as the 51st State of the Union. Congratulations! 

As the newest star on the flag, the State of ISS will receive all the rights, privileges, and bureaucratic headaches associated with American statehood. Please prepare to collect federal income tax, hold primary elections in the cupola, and immediately lower your speed limit from 17,500 miles per hour to a more reasonable 65 mph. 

Furthermore, you are required by federal law to immediately adopt a State Bird (we have provisionally assigned you the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor), a State Flower (Space Cabbage), and a State Motto (“*Zero Gravity, Zero State Income Tax*”). You will also be sending two Senators to Washington, D.C., though they will have to attend committee hearings via spotty Zoom connections.

However, the most pressing matter of your statehood concerns collegiate athletics. 

As a U.S. state, you are geographically obligated to establish a flagship public university and field a Division I FBS college football team. Effective immediately, the University of the International Space Station (UISS) "Fighting Cosmonauts" have been assigned to the **Big Ten Conference**. 

We know this might seem geographically perplexing. However, since the Big Ten recently expanded to include California, Washington, and Oregon, the conference commissioner decided that extending media markets into Low Earth Orbit was the only logical next step for television rights.

Your home games will be broadcast on Fox at Noon EST. We realize that fielding a 115-man roster in a space station essentially the size of a six-bedroom house will be a logistical challenge, but we believe your home-field microgravity advantage will be devastating to Ohio State’s run defense. Please ensure your stadium complies with NCAA regulations, and try to avoid accidentally punting the football into the vacuum of space.

Welcome to the United States. We look forward to seeing the ISS flag flying high, and we expect a very competitive showing at your inaugural homecoming game against Rutgers. 

May God bless the United States, and may God bless the Great State of the International Space Station.

Sincerely,

*The Office of Intergovernmental Affairs*
**United States Government**
